findings.evidence: First section: "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day." Second section: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period. Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.violation: The document contains two separate sections titled or functioning as program overview, with overlapping information about reimbursement logs and how staff access them. This duplication creates confusion about where readers should look for information.
findings.fix: Consolidate the two overview sections into a single section that explains the reimbursement log publication, when it occurs (quarterly vs after enrollment), and how staff can access it. Remove one of the duplicative sections.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: The sentence switches from second person "You must" to first person "we may," creating inconsistent voice and unclear responsibility assignment.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "You must keep your equipment in good working condition. We may request a brief photo check once a year" or "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a photo check once a year."

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.violation: This sentence describes a specific operational problem (backup reviewer not informed) in a policy document, making unclear whether this is an intentional policy or a documented defect. The causality is also unclear.
findings.fix: Either move this to an "Known Issues" section if it is a temporary problem, or rewrite it as a policy requirement: "The designated manager or backup reviewer must sign off before the portal releases the confirmation email. To prevent delays, ensure the backup reviewer is informed of this requirement when the primary reviewer is unavailable."

findings.location: Lines 33 and 27, "Required Documentation" and "Approval Timeline" sections
findings.evidence: Line 27 says "The manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list." Line 33 says "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.violation: The document contradicts itself about whether manager approval follows a standard list or allows discretion that overrides the checklist.
findings.fix: Clarify the hierarchy: either state that managers must follow the approved list without exception, or state that managers have discretion and explain what constraints limit that discretion (e.g., "up to budget remaining this quarter").

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.violation: This phrasing is awkward and unclear. Readers cannot tell if "at this point in time" refers to when the employee made the purchase, when the request was submitted, or when reimbursement occurs.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The finance office deposits the reimbursement amount to offset costs the employee paid at purchase" or "to offset the employee's out-of-pocket expense."

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is used three times in two sentences without clear definition, making it unclear whether an employee can request multiple items or whether each request is a single item.
findings.fix: Define the term once at the start of the document (e.g., "A stipend item is a single piece of equipment the employee is requesting reimbursement for"), then use "item" or "request" in context rather than repeating "stipend item."

findings.evidence: "The portal walks through each step in order."
findings.violation: The sentence uses the vague phrase "in order" without explaining what that order is or why it matters to the employee.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "The portal guides you through required steps in this sequence: confirm eligibility, upload receipt, select equipment category, submit for approval."
